name: willett-hw
title: Implant handwriting (T5, Willett et al. 2021): causal TCN CTC character decoder of our own (P15-08 run R-all-s0) - WEAK, descriptive only
task: attempted-handwriting character decoding, CTC over the 98 P11-01 key tokens (Willett text uses letters, space and . , ' ? only)

input.kind: threshold crossings of two 96-electrode Utah arrays (participant T5, hand knob area)
input.features: raw threshold-crossing counts per 10 ms bin; the runtime z-scores them with fixed per-session statistics (non-test sentences of the session)
input.file_note: one session folder Datasets/t5.YYYY.MM.DD (its sentences.mat; needs scipy); one stream per sentence, from the go cue to the sentence end plus up to 1 s of tail. Only the 10 sessions below have a z-score; a new session needs its own statistics (not in this model)

licence.weights_status: CC0 1.0 (user decision D11, 2026-11-22; data CC0, our own code and training). Not released yet: the upload as a GitHub release asset (D10) waits for a final user yes (P14-02, gap 98). Never in the wheel or the git repository
licence.attribution: Data: Willett, Avansino, Hochberg, Henderson, Shenoy, Nature 593, 249-254 (2021), handwriting BCI dataset (CC0 1.0, Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.wh70rxwmv)
licence.notes: clean track: random init, trained on Willett CC0 data only (run licence.json: research_only false). The research-only T / E / S trunks of P15-08 (emg2qwerty-derived) are not used.

text_files.eng_tatoeba_6gram_mkn_noE2Q_noWillett.np: CC-BY-2.0-FR (6-gram character LM built from Tatoeba English sentences (P15-38: the P11-11 recipe with every emg2qwerty prompt and every Willett text blocked; no Willett text in its train or held-out text); attribution: Sentences from Tatoeba (https://tatoeba.org), by the Tatoeba contributors, CC BY 2.0 FR). Used only by the opt-in LM readout. Local file only, never in the wheel or the git repository: its build blocklist holds research-only emg2qwerty texts (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), so the file is not released before a licence review. The LM text itself is CC BY 2.0 FR

training.data: Willett handwriting 2021 (T5), sentences.mat of 10 sessions: all 781 pool sentences (506.0 min of writing time)
training.split: P15-08 make_splits, salt fidetype-p15-08-2026-11-19: test = last block of each session (80 sentences, 3,448 characters); val = one other block per session (106 sentences); pool = the rest
training.run: derived/p15-08/runs/R-ball-s0 (arm R = random init, budget all, seed 0), final step 3000 (experiments/2026-11-19-p15-08-e1-cross-body)

metrics.name: greedy CER (no LM)
metrics.split: test blocks of the 10 sessions (80 sentences, 3,448 characters, pooled)

metrics.name: greedy CER (no LM), best-val step 2700 (not this checkpoint)
greedy CER of the same recipe, seed 1 (R-all-s1, not released)

limits: Weak decoder: greedy test CER 0.305. The published Willett et al. 2021 real-time decoder is much better (other recipe).
Unstable recipe: the same recipe on seed 1 gives test CER 0.920 (training failed). One good seed is not a reliable method.

No language model in the default readout (greedy CTC). The opt-in LM readout (readouts.lm, P14-48 / P14-49 / P14-50) uses a Tatoeba 6-gram with every Willett text blocked (CC BY 2.0 FR, attribution: the Tatoeba contributors; local only, because its blocklist holds research-only emg2qwerty texts): test CER 0.177 with the gate (P14-59 threshold lo 0.566; 3 / 80 real test inputs gated), no test overlap. Its no-signal gate stops flat, empty and time-shuffled input (time-shuffled 0 / 80 emit text), but not frame-shuffled decoder frames; only the guard offer gate (P14-54, P14-59) stops those offers, the readout text itself is not gated by frame order.

Direction gate (offer gate lm_beam_direction >= 0, both guards): the built-in guard was tested on training data only. With the fixed threshold 0 it passed on the 781 sentences that trained the decoder (time-reversed frames offered 1 / 781, real offers removed 1 / 781); the dataset has no unused sentences, so no test on new data was possible. Treat it as weakly tested. The LM guard passed on the same sentences (0 / 781, 0 / 781). The gate needs the local LM file.
Descriptive only: an offline replay of one participant (T5); not a user study and not a clinical claim.
Only the 10 sessions of the dataset: a new session or participant needs its own z-score statistics and probably retraining.

Other split than the benchmark track willett-hw (last 3 sessions): 193 of that track's 254 test trials were in this model's training pool. Score this model only on its own test blocks (the last block of each session), or retrain it on the track's train split first.

offer_gate.note: P14-54 (plan 09def1e): fitted on the 66 non-LTT val sentences only (threshold = the smallest real offer value); withholds an OFFER when the frame-order coherence is below the threshold; never changes a COMMIT

P14-60 (gap 190; user decision 2026-11-23, option C for gap 181): the P5-36b two-direction LM-beam score with the P5-37 fixed threshold 0 (no fit); withholds an OFFER when the frames decode better time-reversed than forward; never changes a COMMIT. Evidence: P5-37 (results 2451892, decoder-seen pool, weak), P5-36b (results a7bfbc8)
offer_gate.card: direction gate: the frames are decoded forward and time-reversed with the LM readout (beam 8, without its no-signal gate); an offer stays only if D = (S(x) - S(rev x)) / ((n(x) + n(rev x)) / 2 + 1) >= 0. Fixed threshold 0, not fitted. Cost: two extra LM beam searches per offer that passes the coherence gate (median 0.08-0.25 s per offer on one CPU core). Needs the local LM file. Tested on training data only: with threshold 0 it passed on the 781 sentences the decoder was trained on (time-reversed frames offered 1 / 781, real offers removed 1 / 781). No test on unseen data used this fixed rule before it shipped; on the 80 test sentences, looked at after the fact, it gives time-reversed offers 1 / 80 and real offers removed 1 / 80

offer_control.rule: P5-31, docs/trust-guarantee.md section 5a: a control passes if null offer rate <= 0.5 x real offer rate, and (null offers <= floor(0.05 n) or one-sided Fisher exact p <= 0.05); real = the LTT items
offer_control.effect: with the P14-60 offer-gate list (coherence, then lm_beam_direction >= 0; on by default): the guard withholds offers on frame-shuffled, time-reversed and other no-evidence input; commits, config_id and the status do not change (offer-only, 0 LTT commits). Coherence gate only (previous re-check, experiments/2026-11-21-p14-54-willett-order-gate/results/recheck-builtin-gated.json): the same null counts

trust.input: the log_probs (T, 98) of a decode() stream: guard.decide(stream.log_probs)
trust.commits: never: OFFER / WITHHOLD only. The 106 val sentences give 40 LTT items; alpha 0.05, delta 0.1 needs at least 45, so no commit threshold is certified (feasible: false). Test blocks: 0 commits, 77 offers, 3 withholds of 80; safe WPM v0.1 0.00 (vacuous)
trust.null_controls: calibrate: uniform 0/300, frame-shuffled 0/300, time-shuffled input 0/106 commits (all pass); test: time-shuffled and zero input 0/80 commits each. Offers with the P14-54 offer gate (test): real 77/80, time-shuffled 1/80, zero 0/80, uniform 0/80, frame-shuffled 0/80 (without the gate: frame-shuffled 77/80). With the P14-60 gate list (coherence, then lm_beam_direction >= 0; test already used, information only): real 76/80 (1 removed by the direction gate), time-reversed frames after the decoder 1/80 (77/80 with coherence only); experiments/2026-11-23-p14-60-ship-direction-gate/results/wiring.json

trust_note: Offer-only guard (P14-41): it never commits. A guard that can commit needs about 120 or more calibration sentences and a stronger text decoder (word LM: gap 26 = P14-12; stronger decoder: gap 120 = P15-33). The offer list is not certified. Without the offer gate it offers as often on frame-shuffled decoder frames as on real input (77 / 80); with the P14-54 offer gate (trust.offer_gate, coherence, on by default) it offers on 0 / 80 frame-shuffled test inputs and still on 77 / 80 real ones.

lm.status: opt-in: m.text(stream, readout="lm"); m.text(stream) stays greedy
lm.lm_source: experiments/2026-11-20-p15-38-e1-lm-willett-blocked (derived/p15-38); the only LM of this readout and so its default (P14-50). The P14-48 LM eng_tatoeba_6gram_mkn_noE2Q.npz held 13 of the 80 test sentences and is no longer used
lm.settings_source: P15-25 decoder F (fixed before its run; experiments/2026-11-20-p15-25-e1-same-lm/config.json)
lm.gate_rule: kind score, feature logit (P14-49 candidate C5): pass iff greedy CTC emissions n_keys >= 1, n_keys / (0.01 T) <= r_max, and intercept + coef . (z - mean) / scale >= lo, with z = (peak, neg_entropy, nb_share, kps, log(1 + n_keys)) of fidetype.pretrained.lmreadout.posterior_features. Fitted on the 66 non-LTT val sentences (calibrate order, seed 0): L2 logistic regression of real vs time-shuffled input (ridge 1), r_max = 2 x the largest real rate. Chosen among 6 candidates by a pre-registered 2-fold rule on the same 66 val sentences (test never used). lo (P14-58 quantile_lo rule, shipped by P14-59 on 2026-11-22): lo = max(HD_0.03(real S scores), Q_0.99(726 val time-shuffled scores)) = 0.5659 (was the smallest real score, -1.1697)
lm.gate_source: experiments/2026-11-20-p14-49-willett-gate-blocked-lm (val only; the P14-48 count gate k_min 7, 0.425 <= kps <= 2.834 is replaced); lo from experiments/2026-11-21-p14-57-direction-aware-offer/results/p58-rule.json (P14-58), shipped after the three re-checks of experiments/2026-11-22-p14-59-ship-lo (P14-59)
lm.licence: LM text CC BY 2.0 FR (Tatoeba contributors, attribution required); see licence.text_files

metrics.source: experiments/2026-11-20-p14-49-willett-gate-blocked-lm/results.md (ungated, greedy, val); experiments/2026-11-22-p14-59-ship-lo/results/results.json (gated with lo 0.5659; with the old lo -1.1697: CER 0.1746, 1 / 80 gated)

lm.null_controls: test, gated readout (lo 0.5659, P14-59) emits text on: uniform 0 / 80, zero 0 / 80, time-shuffled input 0 / 80 (old lo -1.1697: 2 / 80), frame-shuffled frames 78 / 80 (the gate cannot see the frame order; old lo: 79 / 80). P14-58: 10 new time-shuffled draws 0 / 800 emit (CP95 0.0037; old lo 18 / 800)
lm.warning: the gate reads only per-frame posterior statistics: it stops flat, empty and time-shuffled input on test, but frame-shuffled decoder frames pass it (78 / 80). Treat a text from this readout as a suggestion, not as evidence that the signal was read
lm.test_overlap: none: the LM is built with every Willett text blocked (P15-38: 0 exact, 0 containment matches in its train and held-out text). The P14-48 LM held 13 of the 80 test sentences (5 of 47 unique texts)
